<ul class="mw-collapsible-content" style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; line-height: inherit;"><li style="line-height: inherit; margin: 0">1968<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup>–1969:<sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup> Chair of the <a href="/wiki/Republican_Governors_Association" title="Republican Governors Association">Republican Governors Association</a>
</li></ul>
</div></td></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-below" style="border-top: 1px solid right; font-size: 95%"><div></div></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><b>Ronald Wilson Reagan</b> (<span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="/ˈ/: primary stress follows">ˈ</span><span title="&#39;r&#39; in &#39;rye&#39;">r</span><span title="/eɪ/: &#39;a&#39; in &#39;face&#39;">eɪ</span><span title="/ɡ/: &#39;g&#39; in &#39;guy&#39;">ɡ</span><span title="/ən/: &#39;on&#39; in &#39;button&#39;">ən</span></span>/</a></span></span> <a href="/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key" title="Help:Pronunciation respelling key"><i title="English pronunciation respelling"><span style="font-size:90%">RAY</span>-gən</i></a>; February 6, 1911&#160;&#8211;&#32;June 5, 2004) was an American politician and actor who served as the 40th <a href="/wiki/President_of_the_United_States" title="President of the United States">president of the United States</a> from 1981 to 1989. A member of the <a href="/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States)" title="Republican Party (United States)">Republican Party</a>, his presidency constituted the <a href="/wiki/Reagan_era" title="Reagan era">Reagan era</a>, and he was considered one of the most prominent <a href="/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States" title="Conservatism in the United States">conservative</a> figures in the <a href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States.</a>
</p><p>Reagan graduated from <a href="/wiki/Eureka_College" title="Eureka College">Eureka College</a> in 1932 and began to work as a <a href="/wiki/Sports_commentator" title="Sports commentator">sports broadcaster</a> in <a href="/wiki/Iowa" title="Iowa">Iowa.</a> In 1937, Reagan moved to <a href="/wiki/California" title="California">California,</a> where he became a well-known film actor. From 1947 to 1952, Reagan served as the <a href="/wiki/President_(corporate_title)" title="President (corporate title)">president</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild" title="Screen Actors Guild">Screen Actors Guild.</a> In the 1950s, he worked in <a href="/wiki/Television" title="Television">television</a> and spoke for <a href="/wiki/General_Electric" title="General Electric">General Electric</a>. From 1959 to 1960, he again served as the Screen Actors Guild's president. In 1964, "<a href="/wiki/A_Time_for_Choosing" title="A Time for Choosing">A Time for Choosing</a>" gave Reagan attention as a new conservative figure. He was <a href="/wiki/1966_California_gubernatorial_election" title="1966 California gubernatorial election">elected governor of California in 1966</a>. During <a href="/wiki/Governorship_of_Ronald_Reagan" title="Governorship of Ronald Reagan">his governorship</a>, he raised <a href="/wiki/Tax" title="Tax">taxes,</a> turned the state budget deficit into a surplus, and cracked down harshly on university protests. After challenging and nearly defeating <a href="/wiki/Incumbent" title="Incumbent">incumbent</a> president <a href="/wiki/Gerald_Ford" title="Gerald Ford">Gerald Ford</a> in the <a href="/wiki/1976_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries" title="1976 Republican Party presidential primaries">1976 Republican presidential primaries</a>, Reagan won the Republican <a href="/wiki/Nomination" title="Nomination">nomination</a> and then a <a href="/wiki/Landslide_victory" title="Landslide victory">landslide victory</a> over incumbent <a href="/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States)" title="Democratic Party (United States)">Democratic</a> president <a href="/wiki/Jimmy_Carter" title="Jimmy Carter">Jimmy Carter</a> in the <a href="/wiki/1980_United_States_presidential_election" title="1980 United States presidential election">1980 United States presidential election</a>.
</p><p>In his first term, Reagan implemented "<a href="/wiki/Reaganomics" title="Reaganomics">Reaganomics</a>", which involved economic <a href="/wiki/Deregulation" title="Deregulation">deregulation</a> and cuts in both taxes and government spending during a period of <a href="/wiki/Stagflation" title="Stagflation">stagflation</a>. He escalated an arms race and transitioned <a href="/wiki/Cold_War" title="Cold War">Cold War</a> policy away from <i><a href="/wiki/D%C3%A9tente" title="Détente">détente</a></i> with the Soviet Union; he also ordered the <a href="/wiki/Invasion_of_Grenada" class="mw-redirect" title="Invasion of Grenada">invasion of Grenada</a> in 1983. Additionally, he survived <a href="/wiki/Attempted_assassination_of_Ronald_Reagan" title="Attempted assassination of Ronald Reagan">an assassination attempt</a>, fought public sector <a href="/wiki/Trade_union" title="Trade union">labor unions,</a> expanded the <a href="/wiki/War_on_drugs" title="War on drugs">war on drugs</a>, and was slow to respond to the <a href="/wiki/HIV/AIDS_in_the_United_States" title="HIV/AIDS in the United States">AIDS epidemic</a> in the United States, which began early in his presidency. In <a href="/wiki/1984_United_States_presidential_election" title="1984 United States presidential election">the 1984 presidential election</a>, Reagan defeated former vice president <a href="/wiki/Walter_Mondale" title="Walter Mondale">Walter Mondale</a> in another landslide victory. Foreign affairs dominated Reagan's second term, including the <a href="/wiki/1986_bombing_of_Libya" class="mw-redirect" title="1986 bombing of Libya">1986 bombing of Libya</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Iraq_War" title="Iran–Iraq War">Iran–Iraq War</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Contra_affair" title="Iran–Contra affair">secret and illegal sale of arms to Iran to fund the Contras</a>, and a more conciliatory approach in talks with <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Union" title="Soviet Union">Soviet</a> leader <a href="/wiki/Mikhail_Gorbachev" title="Mikhail Gorbachev">Mikhail Gorbachev</a> that culminated in the <a href="/wiki/Intermediate-Range_Nuclear_Forces_Treaty" title="Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty">Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty</a>.
</p><p>Reagan left the presidency in 1989 with the American economy having seen a significant reduction of <a href="/wiki/Inflation" title="Inflation">inflation</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Unemployment" title="Unemployment">unemployment</a> rate having fallen, and the United States having entered its then-longest peacetime expansion. At the same time, the national <a href="/wiki/Debt" title="Debt">debt</a> had nearly tripled since 1981 as a result of his cuts in taxes and increased <a href="/wiki/Military_budget_of_the_United_States" title="Military budget of the United States">military spending,</a> despite cuts to domestic discretionary spending. Reagan's policies also helped contribute to the <a href="/wiki/End_of_the_Cold_War" class="mw-redirect" title="End of the Cold War">end of the Cold War</a> and the end of <a href="/wiki/Soviet_communism" class="mw-redirect" title="Soviet communism">Soviet communism</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7">&#91;7&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Alzheimer%27s_disease" title="Alzheimer&#39;s disease">Alzheimer's disease</a> hindered Reagan post-presidency, and his physical and mental capacities rapidly deteriorated, ultimately leading to <a href="/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Ronald_Reagan" title="Death and state funeral of Ronald Reagan">his death</a> in 2004. <a href="/wiki/Historian" title="Historian">Historians</a> and <a href="/wiki/Scholar" title="Scholar">scholars</a> have typically <a href="/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_presidents_of_the_United_States" title="Historical rankings of presidents of the United States">ranked</a> Reagan among the upper to middle tier of American presidents, and his post-presidential approval ratings by the general public are usually high.<sup id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8">&#91;8&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Early_life">Early life</span></h2>
<p>Ronald Wilson Reagan was born on February 6, 1911, in <a href="/wiki/Birthplace_of_Ronald_Reagan" title="Birthplace of Ronald Reagan">a commercial building</a> in <a href="/wiki/Tampico,_Illinois" title="Tampico, Illinois">Tampico, Illinois</a>, as the younger son of <a href="/wiki/Nelle_Wilson_Reagan" title="Nelle Wilson Reagan">Nelle Clyde Wilson</a> and <a href="/wiki/Jack_Reagan" title="Jack Reagan">Jack Reagan</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKengor20045_9-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKengor20045-9">&#91;9&#93;</a></sup> Nelle was committed to the <a href="/wiki/Disciples_of_Christ" class="mw-redirect" title="Disciples of Christ">Disciples of Christ</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKengor200412_10-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKengor200412-10">&#91;10&#93;</a></sup> which believed in the <a href="/wiki/Social_Gospel" title="Social Gospel">Social Gospel</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESpitz201836_11-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpitz201836-11">&#91;11&#93;</a></sup> She led <a href="/wiki/Prayer" title="Prayer">prayer</a> meetings and ran mid-week prayers at her church when the <a href="/wiki/Pastor" title="Pastor">pastor</a> was out of town.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKengor200412_10-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKengor200412-10">&#91;10&#93;</a></sup> Reagan credited her spiritual influence<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKengor200448_12-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKengor200448-12">&#91;12&#93;</a></sup> and he became a <a href="/wiki/Christianity" title="Christianity">Christian.</a><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKengor200410_13-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKengor200410-13">&#91;13&#93;</a></sup> According to Stephen Vaughn, Reagan's values came from his pastor, and the First Christian Church's religious, economic and social positions "coincided with the words, if not the beliefs of the latter-day Reagan".<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEVaughn1995109_14-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVaughn1995109-14">&#91;14&#93;</a></sup> Jack focused on making <a href="/wiki/Money" title="Money">money</a> to take care of the family,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKengor20045_9-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKengor20045-9">&#91;9&#93;</a></sup> but this was complicated by his <a href="/wiki/Alcoholism" title="Alcoholism">alcoholism.</a><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrands201510_15-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrands201510-15">&#91;15&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Neil_Reagan" title="Neil Reagan">Neil Reagan</a> was Reagan's older brother.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKengor20044_16-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKengor20044-16">&#91;16&#93;</a></sup> Together, they lived in <a href="/wiki/Chicago" title="Chicago">Chicago</a>, <a href="/wiki/Galesburg,_Illinois" title="Galesburg, Illinois">Galesburg</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Monmouth,_Illinois" title="Monmouth, Illinois">Monmouth</a> before returning to Tampico. In 1920, they settled in <a href="/wiki/Dixon,_Illinois" title="Dixon, Illinois">Dixon, Illinois</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPemberton19985_17-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPemberton19985-17">&#91;17&#93;</a></sup> living in <a href="/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Boyhood_Home" title="Ronald Reagan Boyhood Home">a house</a> near the <a href="/wiki/H._C._Pitney_Variety_Store_Building" title="H. C. Pitney Variety Store Building">H. C. Pitney Variety Store Building</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEWoodard20124_18-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWoodard20124-18">&#91;18&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ronald_Reagan_in_football_uniform_on_field_at_Eureka_College_in_Eureka,_Illinois.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Ronald_Reagan_in_football_uniform_on_field_at_Eureka_College_in_Eureka%2C_Illinois.jpg/120px-Ronald_Reagan_in_football_uniform_on_field_at_Eureka_College_in_Eureka%2C_Illinois.jpg" decoding="async" width="120" height="179" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Ronald_Reagan_in_football_uniform_on_field_at_Eureka_College_in_Eureka%2C_Illinois.jpg/180px-Ronald_Reagan_in_football_uniform_on_field_at_Eureka_College_in_Eureka%2C_Illinois.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Ronald_Reagan_in_football_uniform_on_field_at_Eureka_College_in_Eureka%2C_Illinois.jpg/240px-Ronald_Reagan_in_football_uniform_on_field_at_Eureka_College_in_Eureka%2C_Illinois.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2686" data-file-height="4000" /></a><figcaption>Reagan at Eureka</figcaption></figure>
<p>Reagan attended <a href="/wiki/Dixon_High_School_(Illinois)" title="Dixon High School (Illinois)">Dixon High School</a>, where he developed interests in <a href="/wiki/Drama" title="Drama">drama</a> and <a href="/wiki/American_football" title="American football">football.</a><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrands201514_19-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrands201514-19">&#91;19&#93;</a></sup> His first job involved working as a <a href="/wiki/Lifeguard" title="Lifeguard">lifeguard</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Rock_River_(Mississippi_River_tributary)" title="Rock River (Mississippi River tributary)">Rock River in Lowell Park</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrands201516_20-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrands201516-20">&#91;20&#93;</a></sup> In 1928, Reagan began attending <a href="/wiki/Eureka_College" title="Eureka College">Eureka College</a><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPemberton199810_21-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPemberton199810-21">&#91;21&#93;</a></sup> at Nelle's approval on religious grounds.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrands201517_22-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrands201517-22">&#91;22&#93;</a></sup> He was a mediocre student<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrands201520_23-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrands201520-23">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> that participated in sports, drama, and campus politics. He became <a href="/wiki/Student_government_president" title="Student government president">student body president</a> and joined a student strike that resulted in the college president's resignation.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPemberton199810–11_24-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPemberton199810–11-24">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup> Reagan played at the <a href="/wiki/Guard_(American_football)" class="mw-redirect" title="Guard (American football)">guard</a> position for the <a href="/wiki/1930_Eureka_Red_Devils_football_team" title="1930 Eureka Red Devils football team">1930</a> and <a href="/wiki/1931_Eureka_Red_Devils_football_team" title="1931 Eureka Red Devils football team">1931 Eureka Red Devils football teams</a> and recalled a time when two black football teammates were refused service at a <a href="/wiki/Racial_segregation_in_the_United_States" title="Racial segregation in the United States">segregated</a> hotel; he invited them to his parents' home nearby in Dixon and his parents welcomed them. At the time, his parents' stance on racial questions were unusually <a href="/wiki/Progressivism" title="Progressivism">progressive</a> in Dixon.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECannon2000457Mayer201573_25-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECannon2000457Mayer201573-25">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup> Reagan himself had grown up with very few black Americans there and was unaware of a race problem.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPrimuth201642_26-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPrimuth201642-26">&#91;26&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Entertainment_career">Entertainment career</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_filmography" title="Ronald Reagan filmography">Ronald Reagan filmography</a></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Radio_and_film">Radio and film</span></h3>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti">.mw-parser-output .tmulti .multiimageinner{display:flex;flex-direction:column}.mw-parser-output .tmulti
